newsitem.title: USA: New York Power Pool files plan to restructure.
newsitem.headline: New York Power Pool files plan to restructure.

text.p: The New York Power Pool (NYPP), in a move key to the further deregulation of New York State's electricity industry, said Friday it has sent a plan to federal officials for restructuring the state's bulk power market and operation of its high-voltage power grid.
NYPP represents eight power systems operating in the state.

William Balet, Executive Director of NYPP, said the proposal "will maintain reliable electric service for the people of New York State while introducing fair and open competition in the wholesale power market."

The plan was filed with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), who issued an order to deregulate the nation's power industry but left the details to groups at the state level, including local power marketers, brokers, independent power producers, consumer and environmental groups.
The plan calls for setting up three entities: an Independent System Operator (ISO), a New York Power Exchange (NYPE) and a New York State Reliability Council.
The ISO, a not-for-profit corporation, will ensure the reliable operation of the state's high-voltage transmission grid, giving euqal access to all qualified users.
It will also oversee state-wide transmission tariffs, schedule transmission and dispatching of power on the grid.

According to the plan, the ISO will be governed by a board of representatives from the transmission providers, buyers, sellers, and environmental and consumer groups, with no single group capable of exercising control.
The proposed NYPE will provide an independent market for buying and selling energy and ancillary services, with membership open to qualified market participants.
Other power exchanges may be established, and there will be no special relationship between the ISO and any particular exchange.
The New York State Reliability Council will establish criteria to address the particular reliability needs of the State while adhering to national and regional reliability standards.

NYPP's members are: Central Hudson Gas and Electric Corp, Consolidated Edison Co of New York, Inc, Long Island Lighting Co, New York Power Authority, New York State Electric and Gas Corp, Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, Orange & Rockland Utilities, Inc, and Rochester Gas & Electric Corp.
